detailed_results.feedback: The essay provides an exceptionally clear and detailed overview of your internship role, the duration and daily hours, and a comprehensive list of tasks and projects undertaken. The description of the AI platforms (Jasper and Writer) and your specific activities, from onboarding to creating a capstone demo and LinkedIn posts, is very thorough.
citations: I had the opportunity to intern at Navigaite and get first hand experience with AI and marketing.
I was able to participate in a 10 week program where I worked around 6 hours a day.
At my job at Navigaite, I built a full marketing skill set around generative AI while shipping real work.
I started by onboarding to Writer and Jasper , setting goals, and choosing an athletic team as my campaign theme.
Over the next few weeks I completed Jasper Academy and Writer Academy courses, practiced prompt engineering, and used both platforms to draft and refine campaign content.
I built a content calendar , tested Jasper ’s Canvas workflows, and used Writer for rewriting, summarizing, and SEO tasks.

In the final stretch I produced landing-page and email copy , integrated AI workflows for blog and social, polished the agent, and created two LinkedIn posts one reflecting on my journey and another showcasing the project.

detailed_results.feedback: You have articulated a wide range of new skills and knowledge acquired, both in AI agent creation and broader marketing concepts. The detailed explanation of learning about marketing analytics, customer journey mapping, A/B testing, SEO, and the nuances of AI application demonstrates significant growth and a deep understanding of the subject matter.
citations: During my time I learned how to make an AI agent on Jasper .
I also learned a lot more about marketing as I took extra online courses. I gained a deeper understanding of marketing analytics, and how to engage your target audience.
Beyond that, I learned how to define clear personas and pain points, map the customer journey (awareness → consideration → conversion → retention), and pick the right channels for each stage.
I got hands-on with A/B testing, UTM tracking, and reading basic metrics like CTR, CPA, and conversion rate so I could tell what was actually working.
I learned the basics of SEO (keywords, intent, internal links), how to repurpose one long piece into multiple short assets, and how to set goals and hypotheses before launching a campaign.
Finally , I saw how AI can speed up drafts but still needs guardrails, fact-checking, style rules, and compliance so the output stays on-brand and accurate.
Finally , I learned how to build a mock campaign.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay effectively highlights two significant surprises: the necessity of persuading companies to adopt AI and the critical role of human oversight in AI's functionality. Your reflections on these points, particularly the generational differences in perceiving AI and the realization that AI needs human direction, are insightful and well-supported.
citations: First off, I found that our job wasn’ t just about teaching and showing these companies how to use AI but also persuading them to do so.

One of our main jobs when first working with a business/company is explaining that AI is not here to take jobs but rather help make these jobs much easier and being able to complete simple tasks much faster .
During this process made me realize that I myself do not see AI as a threat as much but more as a tool to help you but for the older generations this is a completely new and unheard of concept.
Another surprise I encountered along the way was how AI cannot work correctly without humans.
AI cannot replace humans, it needs humans to direct and correct it. This made me realize that the panic of AI taking over our jobs is not as relevant as we think it is.

citations: I feel that this internship has very much prepared me and helped me acquire new skills.

Another big takeaway that I got was my experience with the usage of AI and completing a variety of online certifications. I also feel that with my mock campaign will be something I am able to show off and talk about during interviews.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay successfully relates your internship experience to two components of the EMPAC model: Matching and Assortment. Your explanations of how Navigaite matches clients with appropriate AI platforms and carefully curates its own assortment of tools are accurate and demonstrate a practical understanding of these business concepts.
citations: Finally , looking back at the EMP ACT model I felt that my internship with Naviagite does directly relate to some of these components.
Starting with matching, one of Navigaite's main goals is to make sure that they match their clients with the right AI platform.
I learned the importance of making sure that we direct and match the client with the proper tools so they can best succeed.

Another component that relates to my work was assortment. I learned that Navigaite put in a lot of effort with picking and buying the right AI platforms that make the most sense with helping businesses become more efficient.
Instead of just buying as many AI platforms as we could we specifically researched and chose the ones that best align with our and our client values and goals.
